value.rationale: These six codes are new distance records, so structural invariants of the exact record representatives are intrinsically relevant for reuse and comparison. The Euclidean hull controls LCD versus self-orthogonal behavior and is a standard ingredient in equivalence algorithms and quantum-code constructions. The profile is unusually extreme: four of the six record parents have hull codimension at most two, one is fully self-orthogonal, and the high-dimensional hulls retain distances \(68\) or \(72\). This is a coherent structural phenomenon across the full reproducible record set, not an arbitrary invariant of one isolated matrix.
